ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r1.claim: The orchard was so devastated that they could not recognize it at first and thought they had lost their way; they soon saw that their prized possession was gone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r1.anchor: All their desires and wishes were dashed to the ground

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r5.claim: At first they thought they had taken the wrong road; after recognizing the garden, they understood that God's punishment had destroyed its bounty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r5.anchor: قالوا إنا لضالون: أي عن الطريق إليها، قاله قتادة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r6.claim: Another interpretation is that they were mistaken in their plan to harvest while intending to deny the poor; “we are deprived” recognizes that their treachery rebounded on them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r6.anchor: بل نحن محرومون خيرها بخيانتنا على أنفسنا.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#2/r1.claim: After examining the scene, they retract their first guess: they were not lost but deprived of the garden's good through their own wrongdoing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#2/r1.anchor: قالوه بعدما تأملوا ووقفوا على حقيقة الأمر مضربين عن قولهم الأول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r1.claim: Seeing the burned garden, they first thought they had lost their way, then realized they were deprived because they denied the poor and omitted the exception.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r1.anchor: {فلما رأوها قالوا إنا لضالون} أي لما رأوا الجنة محترقة قالوا: إنا لمخطئون الطريق

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r1.claim: After recognizing the garden, they admitted they had instead been deprived through their own wrongdoing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r1.anchor: { بل نحن } أي بعد ما تأملوه وعرفوا أنها هي قالوا { بل نحن } { محرومون }

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.anchor: أن هذه الجنة كانت لرجل صالح، حدودا قومه وبلده فقيل إنه من أهل اليمن

NAHHAS:v5p11/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p11/r5.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p11/r5.claim: Someone recognizing the garden said they had not lost the way but had been deprived of its fruit.
NAHHAS:v5p11/r5.anchor: فقال من يعرفها ويعلم أنهم لم يضلوا الطريق ( بل نحن محرومون ) أي حرمنا ثمارها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r2.claim: They then recognized that they were deprived of the expected good because God took it in response to their intention to deprive the poor; God does not change a people until they change themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r2.anchor: الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r3.claim: A calamity softens and leads to repentance for one whom God intends to guide, but increases another person's disbelief.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r3.anchor: وما كان القرع بالمصائب مظنة الرقة والتوبة لمن أريد به الخير

DURR-FULL:v8p252/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says after recognizing the garden's landmarks, they called themselves deprived and afflicted by misfortune.

DURR-FULL:v8p252/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r8.claim: Asked whether the garden owners were people of Paradise or Hell, Qatada says the question burdened him and gives no answer.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p85/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p85/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p85/r9.claim: بل shifts to the more serious point: they had planned to deprive the poor of surplus, but in fact they themselves lost all the fruit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p85/r9.anchor: و { بل نحن محرومون } إضراب للانتقال إلى ما هو أهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r1.claim: Fronting the explicit pronoun نحن, where the passive's subject could remain implicit, signals an additional restriction: they are the ones truly deprived.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r1.anchor: بأن أتي به ضميرا بارزا مع أن مقتضى الظاهر أن يكون ضميرا مستترا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r13.claim: Seeing the burned orchard, they first thought they had lost the way; once they recognized it, they said they were deprived of its yield and blessing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r13.anchor: فلما رأوها أي محترقة حسبوا أنهم قد ضلوا الطريق، وأنها ليست تلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#2/r1.claim: They realized they had been deprived of the garden's fruit because they had denied it to the poor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#2/r1.anchor: أي حرمنا ثمر جنتنا بمنعنا المسكين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say the brothers first thought they had lost their way, then recognized the orchard and realized they had been deprived of its produce.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r2.anchor: قاله ابن عباس وغيره. ثم رجعوا عما كانوا فيه، وتيقنوا أنها هي فقالوا: {بل نحن محرومون}

JISHUMI:v10p7034/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r12.claim: They realize this is their garden but have been deprived of its benefit because they denied the needy their due and failed to make an exception.
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r12.anchor: بل نحن محرومون يعني هذه جنتنا، ولكن حرمنا نفعها وخيرها لمنع المساكين حقهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r24.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r24.claim: They realized they were deprived as punishment for their wrongdoing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r24.anchor: أي حرمنا خير جنتنا , قال قتادة : معناه جوزينا فحرمنا .

MUQATIL:68:17-27/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r10.claim: Recognizing the landmarks, they realized it was punishment and admitted they had been deprived.
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r10.anchor: ثم أنهم عرفوا الأعلام فعلموا أنها عقوبة. فقالو: { بل نحن } يعنى ولكن نحن { محرومون } [آية: 27]

NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#7/r1.claim: They then realized their deprivation was the result of their own wrongdoing.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:26-27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:26-27/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:26-27/r4.claim: They conclude that they have been deprived of their garden because of what they did.

ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r6.claim: They were deprived of the garden’s fruit because they had withheld it from the poor.
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r6.anchor: أي حرمنا ثمر جنتنا بمنعنا المساكين.

RAZI-FULL:v30p79#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#3/r1.claim: They may first have thought they had lost their way on seeing the burned orchard; after recognizing it, they said instead that they were deprived because their resolve to be miserly had brought this loss.
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#3/r1.anchor: لما رأوا جنتهم محترقة ظنوا أنهم قد ضلوا الطريق

RAZI-FULL:v30p79#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, they called themselves lost because they had resolved to bar the poor and assumed they could benefit from the orchard, but realized they were the deprived ones.
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#3/r2.anchor: حيث كنا عازمين على منع الفقراء

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r12.claim: “We are deprived” recalls 56:67 and broadens the story to all harvests: God, not people, determines whether crops flourish; it may also mean “we are rendered destitute.”
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r12.anchor: This verse is similar to 56:67; it reflects the broader application of this story to all manner of harvesting

TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r1.claim: Some brothers first think they lost the way; another recognizes their own garden and says its benefit has been denied them.
TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r1.anchor: أغفلوا طريق جنتهم، وأن التي رأوا غيرها

TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says they had been repaid by being deprived of their garden.
TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم: {بل نحن محرومون} [القلم: 27] حرمنا جنتنا

TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p179#2/r4.claim: The garden’s owners were deprived of its benefit when its crop was destroyed.

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r7.claim: On seeing the ruined orchard, they first say they have gone astray from right conduct in trying to harvest and exclude the poor; then they correct themselves: they have been deprived of the crop.
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r7.anchor: عن الصواب في غدونا إليها بقصد الصرم ومنع المساكين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r1.claim: The exegetes explain that they had lost their garden's fruit because they had barred the poor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r1.anchor: أي: حرمنا ثمر جنتنا بمنعنا المساكين (¬5). هذا معنى قول المفسرين.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says they first thought they had lost their way because they did not recognize the burned garden.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قالوا: إنا أخطأنا الطريق (¬6). وذلك أنهم أنكروها لأنها احترقت.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r12.claim: They first thought they had lost their way, then recognized punishment and deprivation greater than what they had planned for the poor, and despaired of present and future.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r12.anchor: evvelâ yalnız dalâletlerine hükmettiler, sonra da cezâya uğradıklarına, men‘etmek istedikleri miskinden ziyade mahrum bırakıldıklarına hükmettiler
